Chapter Seven: The Weight of Proverbs 31
As winter crept in, our experimenter found herself drawn to one of the most talked-about—and honestly, most daunting—passages in the Bible: Proverbs 31.
For so many people, these verses have felt like the ultimate litmus test for what it means to be a "biblical woman." It's almost like a checklist of impossible virtues—one that can leave just about anyone feeling a bit overwhelmed.
So, she decided to spend a month living out every part of the Proverbs 31 woman's life. Think about it: rising before dawn, working late into the night, managing the house, caring for family, running a business, and still finding time to help those in need—all with a cheerful spirit.
Just reading that list is exhausting. Imagine actually trying to do it!
Every morning started before the sun came up, with a whirlwind of laundry, breakfasts, emails, and errands. But no matter how much she did, there was always this lingering feeling of not quite measuring up.
And isn’t it funny how quickly even the best intentions can turn into heavy expectations? That sense of comparison and perfectionism can sneak in and steal the joy right out of the everyday moments.
One afternoon, after a particularly hectic day, she sat down with a cup of tea and opened the passage again. This time, something clicked. She realized: the Proverbs 31 woman isn’t an actual person.
She’s a poem—a celebration of strength, creativity, and love. The praise isn’t for doing everything perfectly, but for approaching life with courage and kindness.
And here’s something most people miss: the original audience for this poem wasn’t women. It was men—a reminder to honor and value the women in their lives.
Suddenly, the experimenter saw the real point: Proverbs 31 isn’t about creating an impossible standard. It’s about recognizing the beauty in ordinary, faithful living.
By the end of the month, she let go of that pressure to always be “enough.” The real wisdom in Proverbs 31? It isn’t hiding in a checklist. It’s in the invitation to live with purpose, generosity, and true joy.
